hints: Factor 3 from the first two terms: $f(x) = 3(x^2 - 4x) + 14$.
Expand and simplify to find $a$ and $b$.
walkthrough:
Factor 3 out of the quadratic terms in $f(x) = 3x^2 - 12x + 14$:
$$f(x) = 3(x^2 - 4x) + 14$$

Complete the square inside the bracket:
$$f(x) = 3\left[ (x - 2)^2 - 4 \right] + 14 = 3(x - 2)^2 - 12 + 14 = 3(x - 2)^2 + 2$$

State the values of constants $a$ and $b$:
$$a = -2, \quad b = 2$$

hints: A quadratic function on $x \ge k$ is one-to-one (and thus invertible) if $k$ is at or to the right of its line of symmetry / vertex.
Identify the $x$-coordinate of the vertex from part (a).
walkthrough:
Identify the vertex of the parabola $f(x) = 3(x - 2)^2 + 2$:
$$\text{Vertex at } x = 2$$

State the smallest value of $k$ for which $f$ is a one-to-one function on $x \ge k$:
$$k = 2$$

hints: Take the positive square root since $x \ge 2$.
walkthrough:
Take the positive square root since the domain is $x \ge 2$:
$$x - 2 = \sqrt{\frac{y - 2}{3}} \implies x = \sqrt{\frac{y - 2}{3}} + 2$$

hints: Apply $f^{-1}$ to both sides of $ff(x) = 29$ to obtain $f(x) = f^{-1}(29)$.
Evaluate $f^{-1}(29)$ using the formula found in part (c).
Apply $f^{-1}$ once more to solve for $x$, remembering that $x \ge 2$.
walkthrough:
Use the inverse function from part (c) to peel off the outer $f$ in $f(f(x)) = 29$:
$$f(x) = f^{-1}(29)$$

Now solve $f(x) = 5$ by taking $f^{-1}$ again:
$$x = f^{-1}(5) = \sqrt{\frac{5 - 2}{3}} + 2 = \sqrt{1} + 2 = 1 + 2 = 3$$
Conclude that $x = 3$, which is valid since $x \ge 2$.
